blocks.text: The page first closes the preceding campaign against the Khalsa by showing how Jahan Khan kept chasing the Khalsa Singhs while scattered bands answered with sudden counterattacks. Even under pursuit, the Singhs looted from the vanguard and rearguard, avoided being pinned down, and many Singhs withdrew into Malwa, forests, and other hiding places until they could regroup.

It then opens Episode About Hattoo Singh Majhail by introducing Hattoo Singh as a brave Majhail Sikh from the Kanna Kachha side whose night raid went wrong when his horse slipped beneath him. Captured alive and brought before Ahmad Shah Abdali, he is presented as a steadfast Singh who will not yield even when royal punishment is prepared.

Abdali therefore ordered to be crushed by a ferocious elephant, expecting the spectacle to terrify the Khalsa. Instead the elephant would not kill him, and even when Hattoo Singh was fastened for trampling the execution failed, turning the page into the opening of a martyrdom narrative rather than a routine execution.
